title: When in the Hour of Utmost Need
description: When in the Hour of Utmost Need in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Paul Eber wrote these words in German. Catherine Winkworth's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 515.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When in the hour of ut-most need We know not where to look for aid; When days and nights of anx-ious thought Nor help nor coun-sel yet have brought,

lines: When in the hour of utmost need
We know not where to look for aid;
When days and nights of anxious thought
Nor help nor counsel yet have brought,
Then this our comfort is alone,
That we may meet before Thy throne
And cry, O faithful God, to Thee
For rescue from our misery;
To Thee may raise our hearts and eyes,
Repenting sore with bitter sighs,
And seek Thy pardon for our sin
And respite from our griefs within.
For Thou hast promised graciously
To hear all those who cry to Thee,
Through Him whose name alone is great,
Our Savior and our Advocate.
And thus we come, O God, to-day
And all our woes before Thee lay;
For tried, afflicted, lo! we stand,
Perils and foes on every hand.
Ah! hide not for our sins Thy face,
Absolve us through Thy boundless grace,
Be with us in our anguish still,
Free us at last from every ill,
That so with all our hearts we may
Once more our glad thanksgivings pay
And walk obedient to Thy Word
And now and ever praise Thee, Lord.

licence: Public domain: Paul Eber died in 1569; Catherine Winkworth died in 1878.
credits: Words by Paul Eber (1511–1569), translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
